title: Investigating the Structural Mechanisms of DnaT in the PriA-PriB Replication Restart Pathway Using Single-Particle Cryo-Electron Microscopy
content: DNA replication is initiated through two distinct processes: sequence-dependent initiation at origins of replication and sequence-independent initiation at sites distant from the origin [1]. While canonical DNA replication occurs in a sequence-dependent manner at replication origins every cell cycle, sequence-independent initiation is essential for restarting replication at sites where it has failed or where DNA repair is required [2-4]. These events can occur at any location along the chromosome, resulting in the formation of initiation sites with arbitrary sequences, often referred to as "abandoned replication forks." To address this, bacteria have evolved the critical "replication restart" pathway, which initiates DNA replication in a sequence-independent, structure-dependent manner. The key proteins involved in this pathway in E. coli are PriA, PriB, and DnaT. Although the biochemical functions of these proteins are well-understood, much remains unknown about how they recognize abandoned replication forks and work together to recruit the DNA replication machinery.
